claims.statement: catalog/recipes/openwiki packages langchain-ai/openwiki as the host-driven integration: the session's own agent performs the repository research and page authoring with its native tools, while openwiki owns the durable page queue, Claims validation, source-drift handling, and finalization.

A launch of the openwiki stack delivers four things, as the recipe README records: the openwiki CLI on PATH (install.sh: a project-scoped pnpm install symlinked into $HARNESSED_BIN_DIR), the openwiki skill (install.sh copies the package's own integrations/openwiki directory), one stdio MCP server (recipe.yaml: command openwiki-mcp-host, spawned by hatago), and resumable state (persist entry .openwiki at scope project, location host).

Five operations reach the agent — openwiki_begin, openwiki_submit_plan, openwiki_next_page, openwiki_submit_page, openwiki_finish — and the repository brief at openwiki/INSTRUCTIONS.md is read by openwiki for scope and priorities and never rewritten by it.

The recipe carries no provider credential: host-driven runs use the agent's own authenticated model session, and the upstream MCP server (recorded against dist/integrations/mcp/server.js) builds from a tool provider and never reaches needsCredentialSetup or the onboarding gate that the standalone openwiki --init path walks.

The recipe needs no egress at run time: it declares no egress:, the model call belongs to the session's own agent, and telemetry is disabled through env (OPENWIKI_TELEMETRY_DISABLED=1, honouring the DO_NOT_TRACK cross-tool semantics); the install fetch runs in its own throwaway container during provision_tools FIRST_START, before the pod is created (BOUNDARY) and before the EGRESS phase applies the default-DROP firewall, and a host launch has no firewall at all.
A stack that wants the standalone openwiki generator instead of the host-driven integration needs provider env and an inference host in egress: — a different recipe, not a flag on this one.

catalog/stacks/openwiki composes recipes [default, openwiki] with no services and no harnesses field, and lists default explicitly because an AUTHORED stack does not implicitly extend the baseline: extends: defaults to default only for a DYNAMIC (--recipe) stack composed by launcher._resolve_stack, so an authored manifest without extends: inherits nothing.

openwiki integrations install claude cannot be used in a pod: it writes a skill into ~/.claude (shadowed by the profile mount, and invisible to a host launch) and an mcpServers entry into ~/.claude.json (dead config, because harnessed generates MCP wiring into the hatago config); the recipe re-creates both deliverables from the same pinned package.

The skill deliverable is installed from the pinned package rather than vendored: install.sh cp -RLs node_modules/openwiki/integrations/openwiki — the exact directory upstream's installer copies — into $HARNESSED_CONFIG_DIR/skills/openwiki, dereferencing pnpm's symlinked node_modules so the skill is real files under the config dir and guarded by a SKILL.md existence check; this keeps it byte-identical to upstream's install and keeps third-party prose out of catalog/, which tests/test_prose_lint.py gates.

tools: [npm:openwiki@…] cannot deliver this recipe: openwiki pulls better-sqlite3 transitively through @langchain/langgraph-checkpoint-sqlite and statically imports SqliteSaver at dist/agent/index.js:9, so the native addon is required to LOAD the CLI for every subcommand including mcp, and building it runs a dependency lifecycle script that the house pnpm policy's strictDepBuilds: true default-deny refuses without a reviewed allowlist entry.

The build allowlist can only be project-scoped: pnpm v11 rejects allowBuilds from the global config and the allowlist does not apply to global installs, while tools: is a list of pinned spec strings with no way to carry a build approval — hence the project-scoped pnpm install with a one-entry reviewed allowlist (pnpm-workspace.yaml, copied into the install tree before pnpm resolves), the mechanism catalog/base/pnpm/config.yaml itself prescribes.

Measured in localhost/harnessed-claude:latest with pnpm 11.21.0 and recorded in the recipe: with no allowlist, pnpm install exits 1 with [ERR_PNPM_IGNORED_BUILDS] naming better-sqlite3@12.11.1; with allowBuilds, exit 0 with build/Release/better_sqlite3.node present and openwiki loads.

Losing the allowlist fails loudly twice: pnpm exits 1 naming the package, and install.sh verifies better_sqlite3.node exists after the install and exits 1 with remediation naming the pnpm-workspace.yaml path and the allowBuilds entry — because without the addon every openwiki subcommand dies with 'Could not locate the bindings file', which reads like a broken Node install rather than a denied lifecycle script.

install.sh checks its preconditions before its destructive step: the pnpm-on-PATH check and the Node >= 22 check (openwiki declares engines.node >= 22 and fails at import below it) run before the rm -rf of the previous tree, so an unmet requirement cannot destroy a working install; the rm -rf plus fresh re-resolve makes re-runs after a failed attempt idempotent.

The version pin lives in exactly one place, OPENWIKI_VERSION=0.4.3 in install.sh; harnessed update discovers pin-shaped literals in install scripts as opaque pins so the pin reaches the pin report despite not being a tools: entry; and no pnpm-lock.yaml ships — the top-level package is pinned and transitives resolve under house policy (minimumReleaseAge 1 day strict-fail, blockExoticSubdeps, verifyStoreIntegrity).

$HARNESSED_BIN_DIR is <tool-root>/bin in both modes — the pod's ~/.local (one volume covers the bin dir, mise's installs, and $PNPM_HOME) or the host stack's own tools tree — so install.sh derives its install root as the parent's share/openwiki, keeping a host-launch install stack-scoped instead of in the user's home; the bin is a symlink rather than a copy because pnpm's launcher resolves its package relative to its real path.

--host is the authoring agent's identity, not a launcher label: upstream records producerActor = options.producerActor ?? options.host and metadataModel: host-agent/<host>, so the value lands in run metadata and generated provenance; a literal in recipe.yaml would stamp every harness with one agent's name, and the agent doing the writing is claude/omp/codex/…, never harnessed.

${HARNESS} cannot be placed in the recipe's stdio server args because emit.py writes stdio args verbatim (only a url_env URL gets ${VAR} substitution), so the placeholder would reach openwiki intact and fail its isValidHostId check; the openwiki-mcp-host wrapper resolves $HARNESS from the folder-env contract through hatago's inherited container env at spawn time — the one place that works, and honest for all five harnesses because isValidHostId accepts any lowercase name even though upstream's installer knows only claude, codex, and opencode.

The recipe's MCP entry (name openwiki, command openwiki-mcp-host, transport stdio) is emitted into hatago.config.json as a stdio child that hatago spawns and fronts over HTTP; at launch the per-instance config regenerates with the child's cwd pinned to the mirrored container project path, so the openwiki server operates on the mounted repository.

The recipe's install layer is exactly install: script: install.sh — no system: (nothing needs root, so the same script delivers the same result in both modes) and no cache: (pnpm's content-addressed store would make a second content cache key nothing).

The persist entry (.openwiki, scope: project, location: host) makes interrupted openwiki runs resumable: openwiki keeps conversation history, connector data, and the langgraph sqlite checkpoints under its config dir, and harnessed mounts the project-keyed host dir under $XDG_DATA_HOME/harnessed/persist rw at $HOME/.openwiki in the pod, surviving --fresh.

OPENWIKI_CONFIG_DIR={persist:.openwiki} is declarative recipe env rather than a script export because upstream reads the state-dir override at process start; the {persist:<name>} placeholder resolves to the bind-mount target in a container and the real host persist dir on a --host launch, and the schema rejects an unknown placeholder or a dangling persist reference at load time rather than letting a literal {persist:...} reach the agent.

scope: project keys the host persist dir on the git common dir so every worktree of the same repository shares one .openwiki state dir, falling back to workspace scope with a warning for non-git projects; the generated wiki itself lives in the repository as committed Markdown and is not persisted state.

install.sh writes to exactly two harnessed-owned places — $(dirname "$HARNESSED_BIN_DIR")/share/openwiki and $HARNESSED_CONFIG_DIR/skills/openwiki — so dropping the recipe and relaunching --fresh clears both; persisted openwiki state is separate and removed with harnessed-tools persist-prune --recipe openwiki.

The expect block (skills: [openwiki], mcp: [openwiki]) exists because neither deliverable is visible to the assembler — the skill is written by a script into $HARNESSED_CONFIG_DIR rather than declared under skills:, and the MCP server is merged from mcp.servers and reached through the hatago hub; expected_capabilities unions these declarations with everything parsed, and the capability test launches the stack headless, introspects the live instance, and diffs expected against live.
